answer.title: Loan events on a queue and a reminder consumer Lambda
answer.summary: Adds a `LoanEvent`/`Queue` module, a `transition()` in `status.py` that publishes an event per status change, a `consumer.py` Lambda that mails members, and a SAM template with an SQS queue. The acceptance criteria are mostly not met. Reminder mails are still sent in the request path and again by the consumer, `publish_overdue` always raises, events have no id or dedupe, the front desk imports the consumer, and the queue is an in-memory list.
answer.behavior: A member whose loan is due in two days would get two reminder mails: one from `send_reminders` and one from the consumer after the event. The front desk gets a new `POST /remind` that mails directly through the consumer code and bypasses the queue. In production no event reaches SQS, because `Queue.publish` only appends to a list.

merge_risk.why: Double reminder mails, an overdue publisher that always raises, no idempotency, and a queue that never reaches SQS break most acceptance criteria.

effort.why: Several files interact (state machine, producers, consumer, handler, template). The defects only show when the flow is traced across them.

rule_checks.why: The consumer sets `loan.reminded_on` directly, and `LoanStore.give_back` sets `returned_on` directly.

rule_checks.rule: Consumer is the only sender of reminder and overdue mails
rule_checks.why: `send_reminders` and the `/remind` handler both send the mail outside the consumer path.

rule_checks.rule: Lambdas share only the events module
Events carry an id and the consumer dedupes
rule_checks.why: `LoanEvent` has no id field and the consumer keeps no record of handled events.

rule_checks.rule: Exactly one reminder mail two days before due
rule_checks.why: The direct send plus the consumer send makes two mails.

nodes.label: handler (handler.py)
nodes.description: Front desk Lambda entry: GET /late and the new POST /remind.
nodes.details:
Front desk HTTP entry with a bearer token.
- **Imports `consumer`** and calls `consumer.handle` for `/remind`
- Mails directly and skips the queue

nodes.description: Finds loans to remind and publishes overdue events.
nodes.details:
Decides which loans get reminders.
- `send_reminders` now takes a `queue` and calls `transition`, but **still mails directly**
- New `publish_overdue`, which raises

nodes.description: State machine that applies a status move and publishes the event.
nodes.details:
State machine for loans.
- **New `transition()` and `EVENTS`**
- It checks `move` and sets dates, then publishes a `LoanEvent`

nodes.details:
Shared event contract.
- **New `LoanEvent`** without an id
- **New `Queue`**, which is an in-memory list only

Declared in `template.yaml`.
- No DLQ and no redrive

SQS consumer Lambda.

- Reads loans from `api.store`
- Sets `reminded_on` directly

context.relation: The module-level `api.store` is read by the consumer and the handler.

steps.title: Events and state machine
steps.why_it_matters: `transition()` is meant to be the only place a status changes and the only publisher of events.
steps.explanation: Adds `LoanEvent` and an in-memory `Queue`. Adds `transition()`, which validates the move through `status_of` and `move`, sets the date and publishes. The event has no id, and `Queue` is not backed by SQS.
check_questions: Does `LoanEvent` carry a unique id that a consumer could dedupe on?
Does anything publish to SQS in production, or only append to a list?
Can `transition` to OVERDUE succeed for a loan already past due, given that `status_of` is computed first?

suggestions.text: The loan is mutated before `queue.publish`; if publish fails the date is set but no event exists, so the reminder is never retried.

findings.title: Events have no id, so the consumer cannot skip handled events
findings.detail: `LoanEvent` has only `type`, `loan_id` and `on`. SQS delivers at least once, and neither the event nor `consumer.handle` has an id or a record of handled ids. Redelivery mails the member again.
findings.suggestion: Add a unique `id` field (for example `uuid4().hex`) to `LoanEvent` and have the consumer skip ids it has already handled.
findings.effect: A redelivered or batch-retried message sends the member a duplicate mail.

findings.title: Queue.publish only appends to a list; nothing reaches SQS
findings.detail: `Queue.publish` appends to `self.messages`, and no code uses boto3 or reads `LOAN_EVENTS_URL`, which the template sets. The `LoanEvents` queue is therefore never written to, and the consumer Lambda never fires in production.
findings.suggestion: Add an SQS-backed queue class that reads `LOAN_EVENTS_URL` and calls `send_message`, and add boto3 to the Lambda dependencies.
findings.effect: In production no reminder or overdue mail is sent by the consumer, because no event is delivered.
preconditions: The deployed Lambdas use `library.events.Queue` as it is in this PR

transitions.guard: due_on == day-1 means status_of is already OVERDUE

steps.title: Producers: reminders and overdue
steps.why_it_matters: These functions decide when mails and events are produced, and they currently produce duplicates or crash.
steps.explanation: `send_reminders` now calls `transition` and so publishes an event, but it still sends the mail itself. `publish_overdue` is new and calls `transition(OVERDUE)` for loans due yesterday.
check_questions: Once the consumer mails on `loan.reminded`, does `send_reminders` mail a second time?
For a loan due yesterday, what does `status_of` return before `move` runs?

findings.title: Reminder is mailed directly and again by the consumer
findings.detail: `send_reminders` still calls `mailer.send` and then `transition(..., REMINDED)`, which publishes `loan.reminded`. The consumer sends the same mail when it handles that event. A member gets two mails, and the reminder mail is not sent only by the consumer.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `mailer.send` call and the `mailer` parameter from `send_reminders`, so only the consumer mails.
findings.effect: Members receive two reminder mails per loan instead of one.
preconditions: The queue is delivered to the consumer

findings.title: publish_overdue always raises ValueError
findings.detail: It selects loans with `due_on == day - 1`, so `status_of(loan, day)` is already `OVERDUE` (`due_on < on`). `transition` then calls `move(OVERDUE, OVERDUE)`, which is not in `MOVES`, and raises. No overdue event is ever published, and the first such loan aborts the loop.
findings.suggestion: Derive the old status without the overdue check, or skip the `move` check when status_of is already OVERDUE and publish once per loan using a stored marker.
findings.effect: No loan.overdue event or overdue mail is ever produced, and a scheduled caller fails.
preconditions: At least one open loan is due yesterday

steps.title: Reminder consumer
steps.why_it_matters: The consumer is meant to be the only mailer, and it has to be idempotent and independent of the front desk.
steps.explanation: Reads SQS records, loads the loan from `api.store` and mails the member. For `loan.reminded` it sets `reminded_on` itself. It has no dedupe, no per-record error handling, and a store that is a separate in-memory object in a different Lambda.
check_questions: What happens to the other records when one record in a batch raises?
Is `api.store` in the consumer Lambda the same data as in the front desk Lambda?
Why does the consumer write `reminded_on` directly?

suggestions.text: A `loan.returned` event (and any unknown type) is silently ignored; consider logging unknown types.

findings.title: Consumer changes status outside the state machine
findings.detail: `loan.reminded_on = today()` writes the status directly instead of going through `transition()`. It also uses `today()` rather than the event's `on`. `LoanStore.give_back` in `loans.py` sets `returned_on` the same way. Status changes therefore happen in places other than `status.py`.
findings.suggestion: Remove the write from the consumer (the producer's `transition` already set it) and route returns through `transition(..., RETURNED)`.
findings.effect: Statuses can change without an event, so the events and the loan state can diverge.

findings.title: Consumer reads a loan store that is empty in its own Lambda
findings.detail: `api.store` is an in-memory `LoanStore`, and the consumer runs in a separate Lambda process from the front desk. Its store has no loans, so `store.get` raises `KeyError` for every message. This is an assumption about deployment: it holds only if each Lambda has its own memory and no shared persistence exists.
findings.suggestion: Put the loan data the mail needs (email, member, book, due date) in the event, or read it from a shared database.
findings.effect: Every consumed event fails and retries, and no mail is sent.
preconditions: The two Lambdas are deployed separately, as the template does

findings.title: One failing record fails the whole batch and re-sends mails
findings.detail: `handler` loops over up to 10 records, and an exception on one propagates and fails the batch. SQS redelivers all records, including those already mailed. The template sets no `ReportBatchItemFailures` and no dead-letter queue.
findings.suggestion: Catch per record and return `batchItemFailures`, and enable `FunctionResponseTypes: [ReportBatchItemFailures]` in the template.
findings.effect: Members whose records succeeded get duplicate mails when a neighbouring record fails; a poison message retries forever.
preconditions: A record in the batch raises, for example a missing loan

steps.title: Front desk handler
steps.why_it_matters: It couples the front desk Lambda to the consumer and bypasses the queue.
steps.explanation: Imports `library.consumer` and adds `POST /remind`, which calls `consumer.handle` directly. This mails inside the request, which the PR was meant to remove. It also drops the queue, the state machine and any dedupe.
check_questions: Should the front desk Lambda import anything but `events`?
What does `/remind` do when the body has no `id`, or the loan is unknown?

suggestions.text: `json.loads(...)["id"]` raises `KeyError` on a missing id and `consumer.handle` raises `KeyError` on an unknown loan, so both return an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 or 404.
The response says `reminded: True` and 202, but the mail was sent synchronously and nothing marks the loan as reminded through the state machine.

findings.title: Front desk imports the consumer module
findings.detail: `from library import api, consumer` pulls `consumer` (and its `Mailer` and module-level `mailer`) into the front desk Lambda. The criteria say the two Lambdas share the events module and nothing else.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `consumer` import and publish a `loan.reminded` event to the queue instead.
findings.effect: The two Lambdas can no longer be changed or deployed independently.

findings.title: POST /remind sends the mail in the request path
findings.detail: `consumer.handle(...)` mails the member inside the HTTP request, bypassing the queue and `transition()`. The consumer is then no longer the only component that sends reminder mails, and a later reminder from `send_reminders` can follow because `reminded_on` is set only by the consumer using `today()`.
findings.suggestion: Call `transition(loan, Status.REMINDED, queue, today())` with a real queue and return 202 without mailing.
findings.effect: Reminder mails go out synchronously from the front desk, and the member can be mailed twice.

steps.title: SAM template
steps.why_it_matters: It defines how the two Lambdas and the queue are deployed and how the consumer is triggered.
steps.explanation: Declares an SQS queue, the front desk function with send permission and `LOAN_EVENTS_URL`, and the consumer function with an SQS event source. It has no `CodeUri`, no DLQ and no partial-batch response.
check_questions: Do both functions have a `CodeUri`, and does the front desk package include `consumer.py` only because of the import?
Does the queue need a dead-letter queue and a visibility timeout of at least the function timeout?

suggestions.text: Add a dead-letter queue with a `RedrivePolicy` so a poison message does not retry forever.
Neither function sets `CodeUri`, which `AWS::Serverless::Function` needs for a zip package.
The `HttpApi` event has no `Path`/`Method` and no authorizer, so every route is open to the internet; the bearer token is only checked in the handler.

steps.title: Tests
steps.why_it_matters: The tests pass while the double mail, the overdue failure and the missing dedupe are present.
steps.explanation: The tests cover a single reminded event and the consumer mail, but not the criteria. `test_reminders` was only adapted to the new signature.
check_questions: Does any test check that exactly one mail is sent once the event is consumed?
Is `publish_overdue` or a duplicate event tested?

findings.title: No test guards one mail per reminder, overdue publishing or dedupe
findings.detail: `test_reminds_two_days_before_due_once` checks that the direct mailer got one mail and never feeds the queue into the consumer, so the double mail stays hidden. `publish_overdue` has no test, and `test_consumer` sends a single event only, so duplicates are not tested.
findings.suggestion: Add tests that run `send_reminders` plus the consumer and expect one mail in total, call `publish_overdue`, and deliver the same event twice.
findings.effect: The broken criteria can be merged with a green build.

asks.text: Every status change goes through the state machine in `status.py`, only there, one event per change
asks.why: `transition()` does it for reminders, but the consumer writes `reminded_on` and `LoanStore.give_back` writes `returned_on` directly.

asks.text: The reminder consumer is the only component that sends reminder and overdue mails
Front desk and consumer are deployed separately and share only the events module
Each event has an id and the consumer skips events it already handled
asks.why: `LoanEvent` has no id and `consumer.handle` keeps no record of handled events.

asks.text: A member still gets exactly one reminder mail two days before due
asks.why: `send_reminders` mails and the consumer mails again for the published event.

asks.text: Mails move out of the request path via a queue
asks.why: The template declares a queue, but `Queue.publish` is an in-memory list and `/remind` mails in the request.

asks.text: New POST /remind endpoint on the front desk
asks.why: Adds an endpoint that mails synchronously, which the task does not ask for.

access.auth: IAM (added by the SAM SQS event source)

checked.note: SQS send policy is granted but nothing uses it
